title: Sheafifying an actual finite-free affine ring resolution
statement: Let U be an affine open of a scheme T [def-pc-scheme], and C a cochain complex of quasi-coherent O_U-modules [def-pc-derived-category]. Write A=Γ(U,O_U). Let d be a natural number and P a cochain complex of A-modules whose terms vanish above d and are finite free [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Given an actual quasi-isomorphism f:P→Γ(U,C) (global sections taken termwise), there exists a complex Q of O_U-modules vanishing above d, whose terms are isomorphic to free sheaves on ULift(Fin r) for some natural r in each degree, and an actual quasi-isomorphism Q→C. No pseudo-coherence hypothesis, construction of P, lower bound or geometric morphism is needed.

source.place: Lemma 26.7.5 (Tag 01IB), affine equivalence; Lemma 26.5.4 (Tag 01HV), exactness of associated sheaf

proof.text: Let X=U.toScheme and A=Γ(X,⊤). Construct F=tilde_A followed by restriction along X.toSpecΓ. Global sections of pushforward along X.toSpecΓ identify naturally with the original global sections as A-modules: ΓSpecIso.inv followed by X.toSpecΓ.appTop=ΓSpecIso.hom is the identity. Whisker this comparison with tilde and restriction, then compose the spectrum counit with the restriction adjunction counit. Pushforward along X.toSpecΓ is naturally isomorphic to restriction along X.isoSpec.inv, so it preserves quasi-coherence. The resulting natural transformation Γ⋙F→Id is therefore invertible on each term of C. Naturality assembles its components into an isomorphism of complexes.

For a module map g, the kernel of tilde(g) is quasi-coherent. The invertible affine counit identifies this kernel with tilde of a module. Lift its kernel inclusion through full faithfulness of tilde; its image is a kernel fork, so full faithfulness reflects its limit property. Thus tilde preserves kernels. It is an additive left adjoint, hence also preserves finite colimits and is exact. Restriction along the affine isomorphism preserves finite limits and colimits. Set Q=F(P); exactness sends f to a quasi-isomorphism F(P)→F(Γ(C)). Compose with the counit complex isomorphism to obtain Q→C. Since F preserves zero morphisms, it sends the zero terms of P above d to zero terms of Q.

For each degree n use Module.Free.chooseBasis and finiteness of its basis index, valid also over the zero ring. Enumerate this index by Fin r and reindex by ULift(Fin r). The basis representation is a module isomorphism P.X n ≅ (ULift(Fin r) →₀ A). Apply tilde.mapIso and Mathlib tildeFinsupp. Restriction preserves coproducts and carries the structure sheaf to the structure sheaf via restrictUnitIso; SheafOfModules.mapFreeIso therefore gives Q.X n ≅ free(ULift(Fin r)). These choices occur only in the theorem proof. Combine the bound, degreewise isomorphisms and composed quasi-isomorphism to produce the required existential witness.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01IB and 01IC; the kernel-preservation argument follows the existing Lean proof in AffineDerivedTildeHomologyComparison, and all affine transport and complex assembly are proved here by W2.

from.place: Coherence proof, part (a), finite-free replacement of the affine cohomology complex: transferring its actual algebraic resolution to sheaves

lean.statement:
theorem exists_affine_sheaf_resolution_of_ring_model
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (U : T.Opens) [IsAffine U.toScheme]
    (C : CochainComplex U.toScheme.Modules ℤ) (d : ℕ)
    (hCqc : ∀ n : ℤ, (C.X n).IsQuasicoherent)
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u}
        (U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.obj.obj (.op ⊤))) ℤ)
    (hP : P.IsStrictlyLE d)
    (hfree : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free (U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.obj.obj (.op ⊤)) (P.X i) ∧
      Module.Finite (U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.obj.obj (.op ⊤)) (P.X i))
    (f : P ⟶ ((SheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf
      (.op ⊤)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj C)
    [QuasiIso f] :
    ∃ Q : CochainComplex U.toScheme.Modules ℤ, Q.IsStrictlyLE d ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (Q.X n ≅ SheafOfModules.free
        (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))) ∧
      ∃ e : Q ⟶ C, QuasiIso e
